notes: No class here has a vtable, so there is no +4 shift. The shifts come from bools, containers and one array-limit change.
WWorldPos: identical offsets on both builds; +0x30 is a bool (Xbox byte, PS2 word) followed by padding, so no drift. The three COORD3s sit at a 16-byte stride on both builds.

WCollider: offsets match up to +0x30; PS2 GCC vectors are 12 bytes (+0x30/+0x3c/+0x48), Xbox MSVC 16 bytes (+0x30/+0x40/+0x50); then the PS2 4-byte bools +0x54/+0x58 become Xbox bytes +0x60/+0x61 and the mask moves PS2 +0x5c -> Xbox +0x64. Size 0x68 matches FastAlloc(0x68,'WCollider').

Simulation: offsets match to +0x30; the rigid-body slot limit is 48 on PS2 and 64 on Xbox (AssignRigidBodySlot loop bound 0x40), so the sig table and the owner table each grow by 0x40: PS2 0xf0/0x270/0x330/0x4b0/0xdb0 -> Xbox 0x130/0x2b0/0x3b0/0x530/0xe30 (net +0x80). The simple-rigid-body arrays (96) and the 0x900 block keep their size. From +0xdcc the 12 GCC vectors (12 bytes) become MSVC 16-byte vectors, adding 4 each: tracked instances PS2 0xe5c -> Xbox 0xf0c, trees 0xe68/0xe6c -> 0xf1c/0xf20.

Simulation size 0xf24 is inferred from the last field; no FastAlloc or deleting dtor was found (probably a global/static instance). The ctor reserves 11 of the 12 vectors: grenades (0xeac) gets no reserve call, helicopters reserves only 4.

The Xbox evidence lists +0x4a read by GetRigidBody@0x1c180: that function reads PhysicsObject+0x4a (rigidBodySlot), so it is PhysicsObject::GetRigidBody (a helper), not a Simulation method; its access was left out of Simulation.
MSVC STL on this build: vector = {allocator dword, first, last, end} (16 bytes); the heap tree objects are 12 bytes {allocator byte, head, size}. The allocator dwords are left undefined.

AssignRigidBodySlot returns the slot index (EAX, -1 on failure), not the signature: the existing 'uint' prototype should be int. GetPlayerObject returns cars[0] (a PVehicle*); typed PhysicsObject * to avoid another placeholder.
InRegion, HeightAtPoint, CanSpawn*, FindPhysicsObjectSignature and the second WCollider ctor returns come from sheet semantics or MSVC convention, not from disassembly.
Placeholders RigidBody (0x80, GetRigidBody stride), SimpleRigidBody (0x40, pool split 0x1800/96) and SimRandom (0x10, FastAlloc size) are only created if missing.
